quizzes.title: Year 5 – The Strong Believer
quizzes.description: Hadith of the Strong Believer (Al-Mu’min Al-Qawwi): who is better and more beloved to Allah, taking the means, seeking Allah’s help, and not saying “If only…” (Sahih Muslim). Based on the Year 5 Islamic B lesson.
quizzes.descriptionAr: حديث المؤمن القوي: من هو أحبّ إلى الله، وأخذ الأسباب، والاستعانة بالله، وترك قول «لو أنّي…».

options: The Weak Believer
The Strong Believer
The Silent Believer
The Rich Believer
questions.explanation: In this lesson’s key vocabulary, Al-Mu’min Al-Qawwi means The Strong Believer.
questions.explanationAr: في مفردات الدرس: المؤمن القوي = The Strong Believer.

questions.prompt: Match each Arabic key word from the lesson with its English meaning.
questions.promptAr: طابق كل كلمة عربية من الدرس بمعناها بالإنجليزية.
questions.explanation: These four words are the lesson’s key vocabulary for the Hadith of the Strong Believer.

questions.prompt: According to the Hadith, the strong believer is better and more beloved to Allah than the weak believer.
questions.promptAr: حسب الحديث، المؤمن القوي خيرٌ وأحبّ إلى الله من المؤمن الضعيف.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: The learning objective is to identify who the Strong Believer is from the Hadith: the strong believer is better (khairun) and more beloved (ahabbu) to Allah. The Hadith also says there is still good in both.
questions.explanationAr: المؤمن القوي خيرٌ وأحبّ إلى الله من المؤمن الضعيف، وفي كلٍّ خير.

questions.prompt: Who taught us the Hadith about the Strong Believer?
options: A companion only, without the Prophet ﷺ
Prophet Muhammad ﷺ
An angel speaking on his own
A later teacher with no link to the Sunnah
questions.explanation: The lesson LO is: “Explain the Hadith of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ about the Strong Believer.”
questions.explanationAr: هدف الدرس: شرح حديث النبي محمد ﷺ عن المؤمن القوي.

questions.prompt: Complete the advice from the Hadith: “Be eager for what ___ you.”
options: harms
worries
tires
questions.explanation: The Hadith teaches: be eager for what benefits you — work for good things that help your faith and life.
questions.explanationAr: الحديث يعلّمنا: احرص على ما ينفعك.

questions.prompt: When something goes wrong, what should a believer say instead of “If only I had done…”?
questions.promptAr: إذا وقع أمر سيّئ، ماذا يقول المؤمن بدل «لو أنّي فعلت…»؟
options: “It is not my problem.”
“Allah has decreed, and what He wills He does” (Qaddara Allahu wa ma sha’a fa‘al)
“I will never try again.”
“Someone else is to blame for everything.”
questions.explanation: The lesson and exam mark scheme teach: say Qaddara Allahu wa ma sha’a fa‘al — Allah has decreed, and what He wills He does — instead of “If only…”.
questions.explanationAr: نقول: قدّر الله وما شاء فعل، ولا نفتح باب «لو».

questions.prompt: Saying “If only…” again and again after something has already happened opens the door to the work of Shaytan.
questions.promptAr: تكرار قول «لو أنّي…» بعد وقوع الأمر يفتح باب عمل الشيطان.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ warned against repeatedly saying “If only…” because it opens the door to Shaytan. Accept Allah’s decree and move forward.
questions.explanationAr: النبي ﷺ نهى عن «لو» لأنها تفتح عمل الشيطان.

questions.prompt: Which actions match a Strong Believer? Select all that apply.
questions.promptAr: أيّ الأعمال تناسب المؤمن القوي؟ اختر كل ما ينطبق.
options: Take helpful means (make a plan, practise, ask for help)
Seek help from Allah (dua and tawakkul)
Feel helpless and give up without trying
Keep trying and do not feel helpless
optionsAr: يأخذ الأسباب النافعة (خطة، تمرين، طلب مساعدة)
questions.explanation: SOW key knowledge: the strong believer takes the means, relies on Allah (tawakkul), and avoids helplessness. Feeling helpless and giving up is the opposite.
questions.explanationAr: المؤمن القوي يأخذ الأسباب ويتوكّل على الله ولا يعجز.

questions.prompt: Put these pieces of advice from the Hadith in a sensible order for a believer facing a hard task.
questions.promptAr: رتّب هذه النصائح من الحديث ترتيبًا مناسبًا لمؤمن أمام مهمة صعبة.
options: Be eager for what benefits you
Seek help from Allah
Do not feel helpless — keep trying
If something happens, accept Allah’s decree (do not say “If only…”)
optionsAr: إذا وقع شيء فاقبل قضاء الله (ولا تقل «لو»)
questions.explanation: The Hadith flows from seeking benefit, to seeking Allah’s help, to not feeling helpless, then accepting Qadr if something still goes wrong.
questions.explanationAr: الحديث يبدأ بالحرص على النافع، ثم الاستعانة بالله، ثم ترك العجز، ثم قبول القدر.

questions.prompt: A student trains hard for Sports Day but does not win. Using the Hadith of the Strong Believer, what is the best response?
questions.promptAr: طالب يتدرّب كثيرًا ليوم الرياضة ولا يفوز. ما أفضل ردّ حسب حديث المؤمن القوي؟
options: Say “If only I had never tried” and stop all sports forever
Keep the effort next time, ask Allah for help, and say Allah has decreed what He willed — without opening the door of “If only…”
Blame only the judges and refuse to train again
Pretend trying does not matter because results are random
optionsAr: يقول «لو لم أحاول» ويترك الرياضة إلى الأبد
يستمر في الجهد، يستعين بالله، ويقول قدّر الله وما شاء فعل — دون باب «لو»
يتظاهر أن المحاولة لا تهم لأن النتائج عشوائية
questions.explanation: Exam application: keep trying and do not feel helpless; take the means; ask Allah for help; if the result disappoints, say Qaddara Allahu wa ma sha’a fa‘al because “if only” opens the door to Shaytan.
questions.explanationAr: نأخذ الأسباب ونستعين بالله ونقبل القضاء دون «لو».
